To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a deep network’s predictions are highly correlated with the input features of its base layer; (2) a deep network can be trained to predict a base feature’s importance by using the gradient of its prediction with respect to the feature as the network’s output; and (3) a network’s base layer features can be used to predict a deep network’s output with high accuracy, even if the network is very deep and complex.

(1) we propose a novel method to explain deep neural network decisions, and (2) our method can be used to identify the most important features for the prediction, and (3) our method is more interpretable than existing methods.
